ana: Quick UX note — the percentile toggle on the latency card is confusing. People keep switching to p50 when they actually care about p95 tail latency. Can we add a short explainer or rethink the labels? mike: +1. I keep getting asked by customers why the p95 looks lower after sampling changes. Two quick ideas: rename the options to `Median (p50)` / `Tail (p95)` OR keep `p50`/`p95` but add a help icon with a one-line tooltip. jess: I like the `Median (p50)` / `Tail (p95)` labels for discoverability. Implementation note: adding persistent copy under the chart will increase card height on dashboards (we have tight vertical space). Maybe a compact inline pill or a hover tooltip is better. lee: From an SRE/ops POV we should surface sampling rate alongside the percentile selection. Right now people assume charts are from full traffic; sampling changes across time ranges and can hide spikes. Suggest an inline pill: `sampling: 1/10` that opens a popover explaining effective sample size. ana: putting the sampling pill next to the percentile toggle makes sense. Example microcopy we could use in the popover: `This chart shows 1 out of every 10 requests. Lower sampling may underrepresent tail latency.` mike: agreed. Also let's have the help icon explain the difference in one sentence: `Median is the middle of the distribution; Tail (p95) shows the value that 95% of requests are faster than.` Keep it short. jess: Implementation constraints: the heatmap color saturation is tied to sample volume. If we add sampling info we should also indicate uncertainty — maybe a subtle striped pattern overlay when samples < threshold. That avoids misleading solid colors for sparse data. ana: Mockups: https://www.figma.com/file/abcd1234/latency-dashboard-explainer — I added two variations: `inline pill + tiny label` and `tooltip only`. Which do we prefer? mike: vote: inline pill + tiny label. Tooltip only is too easy to miss. aria-bot: Accessibility check: ensure percentile toggle is keyboard operable and exposes role and aria-label. Tooltips must be accessible via focus and have aria-describedby. Avoid using only hover to convey meaning. jess: Quick ARIA example for the toggle: ```html
sampling: 1/10 ``` lee: We'll also want telemetry events: `latency_card.percentile_changed` and `latency_card.sampling_shown` so we can see how often users notice sampling. I'll add to the telemetry backlog. mike: Decision summary: 1) Rename options to `Median (p50)` / `Tail (p95)` 2) Add inline sampling pill with popover copy 3) Use an accessible radiogroup for the toggle + focusable tooltip 4) Add visual uncertainty treatment for low-sample heatmaps 5) Telemetry events for percentile change and sampling popover open. ana: I'll update mocks (inline pill variation) and post new frames by EOD tomorrow. @jess can you scope the frontend work? @lee can you add the telemetry ticket? I'll draft final microcopy for the popover. mike: :thumbsup: thanks all. jess: I can scope it — estimate 2 dev days to add the toggle labels, pill, aria bits, and popover. Heatmap uncertainty overlay might be another 2 days. lee: I'll create the telemetry ticket and link it here when done. ana: small copy nits to track: replace `Tail` with `Tail latency` where space allows, but keep `Tail (p95)` in compact views. Also include short example in popover: `e.g., p95 = 1200ms means 95% of requests are ≤ 1200ms`. mike: good call. Let's reconvene after mocks. :calendar: next Wed for implementation kickoff. ana: Thanks — will update figma and ping this thread when ready. :sparkles:
